title: IT Business Analyst, Enterprise Applications
jd_text: Role Summary: We are looking for an experienced IT Business Analyst who will play a key role in leading complex technology, ERP initiatives, and the delivery of Enterprise application projects including project support of the latest S/4 HANA solution. The ideal candidate is a results-driven leader who is comfortable taking ownership, pushing through obstacles, holding stakeholders accountable, and ensuring work gets done. A solid foundation in SAP is required, and the familiarity with other ERP systems is a plus; but the focus of this role is delivery, execution, and leadership rather than configuration. Responsibilities: Own project scope, timelines, dependencies, and outcomes, ensuring initiatives stay on track and aligned with business priorities. Review and analyze business processes and make appropriate recommendations for improvement. Translate business requirements into specifications enabling solution delivery. Serve as a liaison between business stakeholders and IT development/support teams Drive integration across SAP and other enterprise applications Work directly with the business users to gather requirements, coordinate and execute user testing, coordinate and execute user training, and provide end user support. Work directly with technical teams to successfully deliver Enterprise Application Projects to manufacturing sites throughout Flowserve. Actively manage risks, issues, opportunities and change, escalating when needed and pushing for resolution. Evaluate ERP and business processes and drive continuous improvement and standardization across manufacturing operations. The ideal candidate combines strong ERP expertise with the ability to enable scalable, integrated solutions across multiple systems (SAP and non‑SAP), while ensuring successful delivery, adoption, and business value realization. Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in IT, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience. 5–10 years of experience leading SAP and ERP-related projects, preferably in a manufacturing environment. Strong knowledge of SAP and end-to-end business processes (finance, supply chain, manufacturing, etc.). Demonstrated ability to own delivery, make decisions, and move initiatives forward in complex organizations. Proven experience managing multiple stakeholders with competing priorities. Strong analytical, organizational, and documentation skills. Excellent communication and presentation skills. Comfortable operating with urgency, accountability, and ambiguity. Solid project management skills 20-30% of travel required Preferred: Experience working across multiple ERP platforms or major ERP transformations. Experience integrating ERP systems with external applications. Familiarity with custom development concepts and system enhancements. Experience supporting multi-site or global manufacturing operations.

title: 26-119.B1 - Sr. IT Systems Analyst (SAP BASIS and Security Administrator)
jd_text: Job Objective: Works with Finance and Accounting, Asset Teams, and the Information Technology Department to understand SAP platform, infrastructure, and security needs; administers and supports SAP BASIS and SAP Security functions; and delivers projects that align SAP technology with business strategy. This role helps ensure that SAP systems operate reliably, securely, and efficiently while meeting business requirements. The position also analyzes, documents, and supports enhancement, patching, upgrade, access, and security-related initiatives across the SAP landscape. This role provides senior-level technical ownership for SAP BASIS administration, SAP Security administration, system reliability, access controls, change management, and SAP infrastructure support. The position works across IT, Finance and Accounting, Asset Teams, business stakeholders, and vendors to ensure SAP systems remain secure, available, well-controlled, and aligned with business needs. Essential Job Responsibilities: Designs, implements, integrates, and supports SAP BASIS and Security solutions with minimal guidance, using strong SAP BASIS and Security skills and a solid understanding of SAP infrastructure. Collaborates with IT, business stakeholders, and external vendors to design, support, and maintain SAP system architecture, security roles, authorizations, and integrations that meet company requirements. Troubleshoots SAP and third-party software issues by working with SAP support, application vendors, developers, and internal stakeholders to identify root causes and implement remedies. Improves existing programs by reviewing objectives and specifications, evaluating proposed changes, recommending enhancements, and making approved modifications. Serves as the project technical lead for system refresh, patch, and upgrade projects. Instrumental in the migration process from test to production using CHARM and TSM Leads the Change Control Board by managing expectations, requiring complete documentation, and ensuring adherence to company change management policies. Administers SAP security roles, profiles, authorizations, user access, and related controls in alignment with company policies, segregation of duties requirements, and audit expectations. Monitors SAP system health, performance, availability, background jobs, interfaces, transports, and related infrastructure components; coordinates issue resolution to minimize business disruption. Adheres to the company’s values – integrity, ownership, urgency, alignment, and innovation. Supports company vision and mission. Adheres to established work schedule, attendance standards and is punctual to work and meetings. Other Job Responsibilities: Builds customer confidence, is committed to increasing customer satisfaction, sets achievable customer expectations, assumes responsibility for solving customer problems, and follows through on commitments. Ensures commitments to business stakeholders are met, solicits opinions and ideas from business and IT partners, and responds promptly to inquiries. Other duties as assigned by management. Qualifications: Fifteen (15) years minimum of information systems experience, preferably in the oil and gas industry, with a strong emphasis on SAP BASIS administration, SAP Security administration, infrastructure support, system upgrades, patching, monitoring, and change management. Interpersonal skills to allow effective communication with individuals and teams. Strong ability in diagnosing and solving problems while maintaining patience, professionalism, and courtesy. Working knowledge of SAP database, operating system, server, and infrastructure concepts related to SAP system administration, maintenance, refreshes, patching, and troubleshooting. Ability to establish priorities, meet deadlines, and concentrate on detailed information in a fast-paced demanding work environment. Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with employees, supervisors, other departments, officials, and the public. Solid understanding of enterprise applications, SAP system landscapes, infrastructure tools, job scheduling, transport management, and general office applications. Ability to complete multiple, diverse tasks of differing priorities with a high degree of accuracy. Proficiency in the use and application of the following software: Required : SAP BASIS Administration, SAP Security Administration, SAP Solution Manager, CHARM, transport management, system monitoring, patching, upgrades, database refreshes, and TSM. Preferred : SAP HANA, ABAP troubleshooting, SQL, SAP Data Services, SAP RISE, PRA, UOM, audit support, and segregation of duties concepts. Education Requirements: Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited four-year university or college with a degree in information technology, computer science, business administration, project management or related field of study, or relevant experience. Certifications, Licenses, Registrations: Formal training in SAP, preferred, but not required Certification in LEAN and/or Six Sigma, preferred, but not required. Project Management Professional (PMP) certification, preferred, but not required.

title: Program Manager, Product Development
jd_text: Be visionary Teledyne Technologies Incorporated provides enabling technologies for industrial growth markets that require advanced technology and high reliability. These markets include aerospace and defense, factory automation, air and water quality environmental monitoring, electronics design and development, oceanographic research, deepwater oil and gas exploration and production, medical imaging and pharmaceutical research. ​ We are looking for individuals who thrive on making an impact and want the excitement of being on a team that wins. Job Description Teledyne Micropac is looking for a Program Manager, New Product Introduction. The Program Manager, New Product Introduction (NPI), is responsible for leading cross-functional teams in the development, qualification, and successful launch of new high-reliability aerospace and defense products. This position drives projects from concept through production release, ensuring technical, schedule, cost, quality, and customer requirements are achieved. The Program Manager serves as the primary interface between engineering, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, customers, and suppliers while managing program risks, product readiness, qualification activities, and successful transition into production. Essential duties to include but not limited to: What you'll do Lead New Product Introduction (NPI) programs from concept, proposal, and requirements definition through design, qualification, production release, and lifecycle transition. Manage and direct the execution of program objectives to ensure technical, schedule, cost, quality, and customer requirements are achieved. Lead cross-functional Integrated Product Teams (IPTs) consisting of Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Operations, Sales, and Business Development personnel. Serve as the primary point of contact for customers, suppliers, subcontractors, and internal stakeholders regarding program status, risks, deliverables, and technical issues. Develop and maintain integrated program plans, schedules, resource requirements, budgets, and milestone tracking systems. Coordinate product development activities including requirements review, design reviews, risk assessments, qualification planning, manufacturing readiness, and production release. Drive timely resolution of technical, manufacturing, quality, and supply chain issues that may impact program objectives. Identify, assess, manage, and mitigate technical, schedule, cost, manufacturing, and supply chain risks throughout the program lifecycle. Develop corrective action plans when deviations from established plans occur and escalate issues to leadership as appropriate. Lead phase-gate reviews including requirements reviews, design reviews, qualification readiness reviews, manufacturing readiness reviews, and release-to-production reviews. Coordinate environmental, electrical, mechanical, reliability, and customer qualification activities required for product acceptance and release. Support Design for Manufacturability (DFM), Design for Testability (DFT), cost reduction, yield improvement, and production optimization initiatives. Coordinate prototype builds, pilot production activities, process qualifications, and transition of products into sustained manufacturing. Monitor and analyze program performance using schedule, cost, risk, and technical metrics. Provide regular status updates and executive-level reporting to senior management. Perform schedule and cost variance analysis, including Earned Value Management (EVM) principles where applicable. Ensure compliance with customer requirements, contract obligations, AS9100, ITAR/EAR, DFARS, military specifications, and company policies and procedures. Allocate and manage program budgets including labor, materials, outside services, travel, and qualification testing expenses. Foster collaboration, accountability, and effective communication among cross-functional team members while resolving conflicts and removing obstacles. Ensure successful completion and closure of programs, including documentation, lessons learned, and transition to sustaining operations. Support proposal development activities, project planning efforts, Basis of Estimates (BOEs), business cases, and product roadmaps. Support, communicate, reinforce, and exemplify the mission, vision, values, and culture of the organization. Occasional travel to customer, supplier, and partner locations as required. What you need Proven experience leading new product development and New Product Introduction (NPI) programs from concept through production release. Strong understanding of product development lifecycles, phase-gate processes, and product launch methodologies. Experience managing technically complex aerospace, defense, electronics, semiconductor, microelectronics, optoelectronic, or high-reliability manufacturing programs. Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams and influence stakeholders without direct organizational authority. Experience planning and executing product qualification activities, including environmental, electrical, mechanical, and reliability testing. Strong understanding of manufacturing readiness, process qualification, production transfer, and supply chain integration. Experience with risk management, issue resolution, and corrective action planning throughout the product lifecycle. Knowledge of program management tools including Microsoft Project, scheduling systems, and resource planning tools. Experience with Earned Value Management (EVM), cost tracking, variance analysis, and financial forecasting. Working knowledge of AS9100, ITAR, EAR, DFARS, and military/aerospace product development requirements. Experience supporting proposal development, project estimation, budget planning, and contract execution. Strong analytical, organizational, negotiation, conflict resolution, and decision-making skills. Excellent presentation, communication, and customer relationship management skills. Demonstrated success managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment. Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Engineering Technology, Business, or a related technical discipline - required Minimum of 7 years of program management, project leadership, product development, engineering, or related experience in aerospace, defense, electronics, semiconductor, microelectronics, or other high-reliability manufacturing environments - required Experience leading cross-functional product development teams and managing new product introduction activities - required Ability to effectively communicate with customers, suppliers, executive leadership, engineers, manufacturing personnel, and technical stakeholders - required Demonstrated experience managing program schedules, budgets, risks, and customer deliverables - required Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Microsoft Project, and program management tools - required PMP certification preferred. title: New Product Introduction Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) Coordinator
jd_text: Forming Our Future together FormFactor, Inc. (NASDAQ: FORM), is a leading provider of essential test and measurement technologies along the full semiconductor product life cycle — from characterization, modeling, reliability, and design de-bug, to qualification and production test. Semiconductor companies rely upon FormFactor’s products and services to accelerate profitability by optimizing device performance and advancing yield knowledge. The company serves customers through its network of facilities in Asia, Europe, and North America. Rooted in our core values — Focus on the Customer, Ownership & Accountability, Respectfully & Effectively Communicate, and Motivate & Develop People — we foster an environment where diverse perspectives are not only welcomed but celebrated. Everyone can make an impact here. Whether it's improving products, supporting customers, or positively influencing peers and the community, the contributions of our people matter. Shift: The regular hours for this position are day shift. Job Description: The New Product Introduction (NPI) Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) Coordinator is the primary operational link between Engineering, the Integration Team, and Manufacturing during the introduction of new products and first articles. The role owns the coordination and accurate setup of new products in PROMIS, Agile, Oracle, and related factory applications; drives the cross-functional readiness and factory-acceptance process; supports engineers in converting technical requirements into executable manufacturing flows and documentation; and trains the Manufacturing organization before product release. You will be responsible for managing system configuration, troubleshooting IT issues, and supporting the implementation of MES solutions. Key Responsibilities: Factory Application and Product Setup Own the end-to-end creation, maintenance, validation, and release of new-product and first-article setup in PROMIS, Agile, Oracle, and other manufacturing applications. Receive new-product introductions from the business unit and coordinate the initial review of existing designs, demand, product requirements, and source-factory information. Coordinate the creation and validation of manufacturing routings, operation sequences, part numbers, bills of material, product structures, revision levels, and supporting master data. Work with Process and Equipment Engineering by manufacturing area to define process steps, equipment requirements, toolsets, recipes, and required controls before creating the factory flow. Verify that each manufacturing operation references the correct work instruction, drawing, specification, recipe, material, tooling, inspection, and quality requirement. Coordinate required application changes with Engineering, Planning, Quality, Supply Chain, IT/Business Systems, and Manufacturing. Deliver high-level training and support end users, ensuring they are equipped to fully leverage the MES system. Serve as the Manufacturing interface with IT and business-system owners for PROMIS, Xsite, INFICON, and other systems needed to execute and monitor the product flow. Perform readiness checks and resolve or escalate system and data gaps before first-article or production execution. Maintain configuration alignment across PROMIS, Agile, Oracle, released engineering documentation, and the approved factory flow. NPI Coordination and Factory Readiness Coordinate the cross-functional introduction of new products from initial planning through first article, learning cycles, and manufacturing release. Develop and maintain NPI readiness plans, milestones, action registers, risk lists, and launch schedules. Facilitate NPI readiness reviews and ensure clear ownership, due dates, follow-up, and escalation of open actions. Coordinate design-for-manufacturability review and confirm that requirements are addressed before material is run. Lead the preliminary review and secure formal factory acceptance of the proposed product flow before first-article material is released. Confirm readiness of applications, materials, tooling, equipment, documentation, quality requirements, production controls, and trained personnel before execution. Coordinate first-article builds, learning cycles, and early production activity; document issues, decisions, and lessons learned and drive actions to closure. Finalize and release the approved PROMIS flow after factory acceptance and completion of required changes. Provide clear status communication to functional leaders and stakeholders. Product Data and Material Readiness Coordinate new-product bill-of-material introduction and ensure required components, consumables, and materials are identified before execution. Coordinate material changes and verify that approved revisions are reflected consistently in Oracle, Agile, PROMIS, work instructions, and production planning. Partner with Planning, Supply Chain, and Manufacturing to establish ordering requirements, stocking strategy, and appropriate minimum/maximum inventory levels for new products. Track material-readiness risks and escalate shortages, master-data gaps, or ordering constraints that could delay first articles or production release. Engineering and Documentation Support Assist engineers in preparing, formatting, routing, and releasing manufacturing work instructions and supporting documentation. Translate released engineering requirements into clear, operator-ready execution steps while preserving engineering ownership of technical content and approval. Coordinate reviews to ensure work instructions accurately reflect process sequence, recipes, materials, tooling, safety requirements, inspection criteria, queue-time limits, and reaction plans. Identify inconsistencies among engineering specifications, application data, work instructions, and actual factory execution and coordinate correction. Support document and configuration change control throughout NPI and production release. Manufacturing Training and Launch Support Develop and coordinate training plans for manufacturing supervisors, technicians, and operators prior to product release. Train the Manufacturing organization on new-product flows, application transactions, work instructions, documentation requirements, and critical quality expectations. Partner with Engineering and subject-matter experts to ensure technical training content is accurate and complete. Maintain training materials, attendance records, qualification checklists, and completion status. Provide hands-on floor support during first articles, learning cycles, and early production until the product is transferred to routine manufacturing ownership. Gather operator feedback and coordinate improvements to documentation, systems, and training. Preferred Qualifications & Experiences: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology or related field, or equivalent experience. Experience in IT, PROMIS systems, or a related industry, with hands-on experience using PROMIS MES systems. Experience creating or maintaining product data, manufacturing routings, bills of material, work instructions, or factory master data. Demonstrated ability to coordinate work across multiple functions and drive actions to completion without direct authority. Strong attention to detail, organization, follow-through, written communication, and verbal communication. Ability to understand technical information and translate it into clear manufacturing execution and training content. Ability to work effectively with engineers, technicians, supervisors, operators, planners, quality personnel, and business-system teams. Experience with PROMIS or another manufacturing execution system (MES). Experience with Agile PLM, Oracle ERP, or comparable product-lifecycle and enterprise-resource systems. Experience with Xsite, INFICON, or comparable factory monitoring and manufacturing support applications. Experience supporting first articles, engineering builds, product transfers, or factory launches. title: Warehouse Lead - Spare Parts
jd_text: The Role The Role At Fisher & Paykel, we create moments of delight together in the heart of the home. Supporting the Warehouse Manager, this role drives a continuous improvement approach and a strong health and safety culture, with oversight of the warehouse and distribution operation scorecard to ensure efficient, cost-effective management of goods. Success in this role requires strong operational knowledge, a commitment to safety, and the ability to lead by example in a fast-paced distribution environment. You Will Planning & Leadership Support the implementation of continuous improvement initiatives, driving strategic improvements and ensuring alignment with company objectives. Support the development of warehouse personnel, helping build the critical capabilities needed to deliver F&P's strategy. Demonstrate a leadership style aligned with the organization's purpose, values, and strategy. Own adherence to and training on standard operating procedures (SOPs). Conduct regular performance evaluations with the Warehouse Manager and provide feedback to sustain high productivity and morale within the team. Foster a culture of teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement among warehouse staff. Prepare regular reports on warehouse activities, including inventory levels, shipping/receiving performance, and operational metrics. Analyze data to identify trends, inefficiencies, and areas for improvement, proposing and implementing solutions as needed. Operations Maintain a clean, organized, and safe working environment in compliance with company policies and regulatory requirements. Supervise and execute daily activities of warehouse staff, including receiving, storing, picking, and shipping parts. Lead quality control measures to ensure accuracy and condition of parts during receiving, storage, and shipping. Support investigation and resolution of discrepancies or customer complaints related to inventory or shipments. Ensure the security of stock and assets by monitoring adherence to security procedures and protocols. Support implementation of inventory control procedures to minimize discrepancies and optimize storage space utilization. Drive a results-oriented operation focused on operational KPIs, accountability, and continuous improvement. Plan resourcing to meet throughput demand and operational KPIs, ensuring optimal performance and cost-efficiency. Ensure adherence to 5S standards within the warehouse, conducting audits and inspections to maintain operational and H&S controls. Oversee warehouse MHE servicing and safety policies, invoice and spend management, and site services including recycling, waste, and utilities. Ensure compliance with labor regulations relative to your area of the DC. Identify and assess potential hazards within the warehouse; ensure hazards, near misses, and incidents are reported, recorded, investigated, and risk-assessed, and implement reasonably practicable controls to prevent recurrence. Ensure all employees, contractors, and visitors receive comprehensive H&S training; conduct regular refresher courses and emergency drills to maintain high safety standards. Demonstrate visible and proactive leadership in H&S, leading by example and fostering a strong safety culture; conduct regular H&S meetings and actively engage with staff. Lead thorough investigations into incidents and near misses to identify root causes, develop and implement corrective actions, and share lessons learned across the organization. Conduct regular safety audits and inspections to ensure compliance with H&S standards, identifying areas for improvement and monitoring the effectiveness of safety measures. Track and analyze H&S performance metrics; report on safety performance and recommend actions for improvement, ensuring H&S objectives and KPIs are met or exceeded.
